display.purpose: Hero title only. Three stacked lines at extreme scale (up to 168px / 10.5rem). Compressed line-height creates visual mass. The scale deliberately exceeds typical heading ceilings — it is the brand making its tagline into architecture.

headline.purpose: Section headings and the CTA card. Maintains Schibsted Grotesk 700 weight; scale differentiates it from Display. The ≥1.6 scale ratio from Display to Headline preserves clear hierarchy.

title.purpose: Card headings, pillar titles. Same Schibsted Grotesk weight and tracking as Headline; smaller size. Used inside contained components.

body.purpose: All prose copy. Hanken Grotesk at 17px with 1.55 line-height for legibility. Full Chalk White (#f3f2f8) for primary copy; 64% opacity for supporting text.

label.purpose: Section eyebrows, card numbers, meta text, pill tags. Space Mono exclusively; capped at 12px. Never used for body copy or anything longer than 6 words.

shadows.name: btn-glow-rest
shadows.purpose: Always-visible violet halo under primary buttons at rest. Establishes the button as the primary action before any interaction.

shadows.name: btn-glow-hover
shadows.purpose: Expanded cyan glow on button hover. The hue shift from violet to cyan signals activation; the increased spread communicates elevation.

shadows.name: cta-ambient
shadows.value: radial-gradient(circle, color-mix(in oklab, #22d3ee 22%, transparent), transparent 60%) with filter: blur(30px)
shadows.purpose: Diffuse floor-level glow behind the CTA card. Structural light source, not shadow. Places the card on a lit surface rather than floating it.

motion.name: ease-magnetic
motion.purpose: Default easing for all interactive transforms (hover lifts, button presses, card elevations). Exponential ease-out gives the fluid, magnetic feel of elements moving toward and away from the cursor.

motion.name: ease-reveal
motion.purpose: Scroll-reveal transitions. Same curve as magnetic; applied at 0.9s duration to create a slower, more deliberate entrance.

motion.name: duration-hover
motion.purpose: Transform and shadow transitions on hover. Fast enough to feel responsive, slow enough to feel weighted.

motion.name: duration-reveal
motion.purpose: Scroll-triggered reveal duration. Long enough for the reveal to feel choreographed rather than instantaneous.

motion.name: duration-subtle
motion.purpose: Color, opacity, and background transitions. Faster than hover transforms; used for state changes that don't involve movement.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Single-column process grid; kinetic hero row stacks vertically.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Work grid collapses to single column; split hero orb fills full width.

breakpoints.name: nav-collapse
breakpoints.purpose: Nav links hide; only logo and primary CTA remain visible.

narrative.overview:
Three Dimos is a web studio whose landing page is also its portfolio, its pitch deck, and its product demo. The design system reflects that double function: every surface must earn its existence by demonstrating what the studio sells — design that is intentional, code that is precise, motion that is alive. The system is dark-first, cinematic, and built around three accent beams (violet, cyan, magenta) that project from a near-black void. Contrast is structural, not decorative. Density is controlled; every section breathes on its own terms.

Typography is the primary performer. Schibsted Grotesk pushes the display weight to 800 at sizes that dwarf a typical heading — the hero title runs to 10.5rem, a deliberate choice that makes the page shout its own tagline. The monospace label font (Space Mono) appears only at small scales as a counter-voice: sparse, technical, anchoring. Body copy (Hanken Grotesk) sits back and lets the headings lead. The three-font stack is a cast of three, not a font system applied uniformly.

Motion is structural. The WebGL background (reef or orb), the scroll-reveal stagger, the kinetic marquee variant — each is an argument, not flair. This system explicitly rejects the 'generic Awwwards fodder' lane: over-animated dark-mode agencies whose technical impressiveness works on other designers but alienates the small business owners who are the actual clients.
keyCharacteristics: Dark void backgrounds with tonal surface lift (no heavy shadows)
Three-color gradient accent that appears as brand signature, not decoration
Ultra-compressed display headings (line-height 0.9) at extreme scales
Monospace labels as counter-voice — sparse, minimal, never dominant
Fluid motion intensity via --motion variable; reduced motion is a zero cost
Glass panels (backdrop-filter blur) used structurally in nav only — never on content cards

rules.name: The Three-Beam Rule
rules.body: The brand gradient (linear-gradient(110deg, #7c5cff, #22d3ee 52%, #ff4d9d)) is the brand's single most recognizable mark. Permitted contexts: logo, hero title selective lines, button backgrounds, short tagline text in service cards, the footer wordmark. Prohibited: body paragraphs, card backgrounds, section backgrounds, nav items.

rules.name: The One Status Color Rule
rules.body: Live Green (#37e39b) is used exclusively as a status signal (booking availability). Never repurpose it as a general accent or decorative element.

rules.name: The Compression Rule
rules.body: Display and Headline headings run at line-height 0.98 or tighter. Never relax display headings to line-height 1.2; that softens the page's intention.

rules.name: The Mono Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Space Mono is capped at 12px and used only for labels, metadata, eyebrows, and pill tags. Never use it for body copy or anything longer than 6 words.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Glows appear only in response to interaction (hover, active) or as structural light sources (hero spotlight, CTA ambient). Never apply box-shadow to a card or container as a 'depth' affordance; use tonal surface lift instead.

dos: Do let the brand gradient carry the brand's visual identity — on the logo, hero title, CTA buttons, and short service taglines. These are the permitted contexts.
Do use tonal surface lift (alternating #07070c / #0b0b13) for section separation. Borders and shadows are not needed when the surface itself shifts.
Do run display headings at line-height 0.9–0.98 and letter-spacing -0.03em to -0.045em.
Do use Space Mono exclusively for labels, eyebrows, and meta at 12px maximum.
Do use backdrop-filter blur on the navigation and floating status elements only.
Do express button hover via the violet-to-cyan glow shift combined with translateY(-2px).
Do wire up the --motion variable (0 to 1.4) to control animation intensity. Every timed animation must scale its duration or disable at --motion: 0.
Do keep body text at full #f3f2f8 for primary copy; use rgba(243,242,248,0.64) only for supporting and secondary text.
Do give cards the cursor-tracking radial spotlight (--mx custom property) for hover depth.
donts: Don't build like generic Awwwards fodder — over-animated dark-mode studios whose technical impressiveness impresses designers but alienates small business owners.
Don't apply the brand gradient to body paragraphs, card backgrounds, section backgrounds, or nav items. When the gradient becomes wallpaper, it loses its signal value.
Don't use backdrop-filter glass on content cards or section containers.
Don't use Live Green (#37e39b) for anything other than the booking availability status indicator.
Don't add eyebrow labels above every section heading. An eyebrow on a self-explanatory section heading is AI grammar.
Don't relax the compressed heading metrics (line-height 0.98 or tighter, letter-spacing -0.03em or tighter).
Don't use Space Mono at sizes above 12px or for text longer than 6 words.
Don't use any standard box-shadow on a card at rest. Depth comes from tonal surface lift and radial face gradients.
Don't add numbered 01/02/03 labels above general section headings as structural scaffolding.
Don't introduce a fourth font family. The three-font stack is a cast.
